Recipe: Chicken Tenders • 1 lb chicken tenderloins • 1 tsp onion powder • 1 tsp garlic powder • 1 tsp seasoned salt • 1 tsp creole seasoning • 1 tsp cayenne pepper (optional, adjust to spice) • 1 tsp all purpose seasoning • 1 sazon packet • 1–2 cups buttermilk • ⅛ cup jalapeño or pickle juice • 3 cups all-purpose flour (season with same seasonings) Hot Honey Sauce • ½ cup buffalo sauce • ¼ cup honey • ⅛ cup hot sauce (optional) Pasta • 1 lb penne pasta • 2 tbsp unsalted butter • 2 garlic cloves, finely minced • ½ yellow onion, finely chopped • 1 ½ cups heavy cream • 1 tsp onion powder • 1 tsp garlic powder • 1 tsp seasoned salt • 1 tsp creole seasoning • 1 tsp cayenne pepper (optional) • 1 tsp all purpose seasoning • 1 tsp black pepper • Grated mozzarella • Grated Parmesan Instructions 1. Ingredients  1 lb chicken tenders For the wet batter: 1 1/2 cup butter milk 2 tbsp lemon juice  2 tbsp soy sauce  1/4 cup hot sauce  Salt to taste 1 tbsp garlic powder  1 tbsp onion powder  1 tbsp smoked paprika powder  1 tsp black pepper powder  For the dry batter: 2 cups all purpose flour 1/2 cup corn starch  2 tbsp baking powder  Salt to taste 1 tbsp garlic powder  1 tbsp onion powder  1 tbsp smoked paprika powder  1 tsp black pepper powder  For the sweet chili garlic sauce  1/3 cup honey  2 tbsp ketchup  1 tbsp soy sauce sauce  1 tbsp fresh lemon juice  1/4 cup hot sauce  1 tbsp chili garlic sauce  3 cloves garlic, minced Salt to taste 2 tbsp butter, cold For the ranch dressing  1/2 cup mayonnaise 1/4 cup sour cream 2 tbsp buttermilk 1/2 tsp garlic powder 1/2 tsp onion powder 1/2 tsp dried parsley 1/4 tsp dried dill 1/4 tsp black pepper 1 tsp lemon juice Salt to taste Method: Marinate chicken with buttermilk, lemon juice, soy sauce, hot sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and salt. Mix well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or 2–4 hours for the best flavor and tenderness. In a bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, baking powder, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and salt. Remove chicken from the buttermilk mixture and coat well in seasoned flour, pressing the flour onto the chicken. Dip back into the reserved buttermilk marinade, then coat again in flour, pressing and squeezing the flour onto the chicken for a thick, craggy coating. Let rest for 5–10 minutes. Heat oil to 350°F and fry in batches for 4–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and the chicken reaches 165°F. Transfer to a wire rack to keep crispy. For the sauce, add honey, ketchup, soy sauce, lemon juice, hot sauce, chili garlic sauce, garlic, and salt to a saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes until glossy and slightly thickened. Turn heat to low and whisk in the cold butter. Lightly brush the sweet chili garlic glaze over the chicken tenders. For the ranch, whisk everything together and refrigerate for 15–30 minutes. Serve with ranch and enjoy #recipe #chickentenders

Butter Chicken Recipe 🍛🔥👇🏼  For chicken:   2 chicken breast   3 tbsp Greek yogurt   Minced ginger   1 tsp garlic powder, paprika, cayenne, salt, cumin   1/2 lemon   For sauce:   1 tbsp butter   1/2 onion   2 fresh cloves garlic   1/2 tsp paprika, cumin, salt and chicken bouillon powder (optional)   2 1/4 cup tomato passata   1-2 tsp sugar   1 cup heavy cream   2 tbsp butter   cilantro   First, we’re going to cut the chicken into small cubes and season it with the spices, fresh ginger, lemon, and Greek yogurt. Then in a pan, add oil and fry the chicken.   Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and garlic.   Once the chicken is ready, remove it from the pan. In the same pan, add a small piece of butter and fry the onion, garlic, and spices together for 5 minutes over low heat until softened. Then add the tomato passata, sugar, and heavy cream. Ingredients  - 1.5 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast - 1 1/2 cups buttermilk  - 1/3 cup pickle juice - 1/4 cup hot sauce - 1 large egg - 1 1/2 tsp garlic powder  - 1 1/2 tsp onion powder  - 1 1/2 tsp chipotle powder  - 1 tsp smoked paprika  - 1 tsp mustard seed powder  - 1 tsp chicken bouillon powder  - Salt and pepper to taste  Dredge - 1 1/2 cups all purpose flour  - 1/2 cup cornstarch  - 1 1/2 tsp garlic powder - 1 1/2 tsp onion powder - 1 tsp smoked paprika - 1 tsp chipotle powder - 1 tsp chicken bouillon powder  - 1 sazon packet (optional) - 1/2 tsp mustard powder - Salt and pepper to taste  - Drizzle of marinade  Honey chipotle sauce - 1/2 cup honey - 3 tbsp chipotle peppers, blended - 1 tbsp unsalted butter - 2 tsp apple cider vinegar  - 1/2 tsp garlic powder  - 1/4 tsp smoked paprika  - Salt to taste Assembly - Brioche buns - Pickles - Ranch Instructions  - Cut/pound chicken into even sandwich-sized pieces and add to a large bowl. - Add butter milk, seasonings, 1 egg, pickle juice, hot sauce, and mix until well combined. Refrigerate for 3 hours minimum or overnight for best results. - Combine all dredge ingredients. Drizzle a little of the marinade into the flour and toss with spoon create those crispy, craggy pieces. - Remove chicken from the marinade and coat well in the dredge. Dip it back into the marinade, then into the dredge again, pressing the flour mixture firmly onto the chicken. Let the double-battered chicken rest for 10–12 minutes so the coating sticks. - Heat frying oil to 350°F. Fry chicken in batches until deeply golden and crispy and the center reaches 165°F. Transfer to a wire rack to drain. - For the honey chipotle sauce, add honey, blended chipotle peppers, butter, apple cider vinegar, garlic powder, smoked paprika and salt to a saucepan. Heat on low for 2–3 minutes, stirring until smooth and glossy. - Brush or drizzle the warm honey chipotle sauce over the freshly fried chicken. - Toast your brioche buns, add ranch, pickles, crispy honey chipotle chicken, and serve immediately.  • • • #recipe #recipeideas #chickenrecipe #sandwich

Ingredients:  • 3 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces  • ½ tbsp garlic salt  • 1 tbsp black pepper  • ¼ cup cornstarch (plus a little extra if you want more crunch)  • 2–3 tbsp vegetable oil (for frying) Sauce:  • ½ cup honey  • ¼ cup soy sauce  • 1 tbsp ginger paste  • 2–3 tbsp minced garlic To Finish:  • Sesame seeds  • Green onions, sliced ⸻ Instructions:  1. Season the chicken In a large bowl, add chicken, garlic salt, black pepper, and cornstarch. Toss until everything is well coated. (Add a little extra cornstarch if you want it extra crispy.)  2. Cook the chicken Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add chicken in batches and cook until browned on both sides with a light crust. Don’t overcrowd the pan. Directions: Season about 6-8 boneless skinless chicken thighs (depending on how many you’re serving) with all named seasonings. Marinate from 1 hour up to overnight. The longer the better. Use a Dutch oven or stock pot to sear the chicken in 2 TBSP of butter or olive oil. Sear for about 2-3 mins on each side on a medium high heat.  Remove chicken from pot. If you see little dark bits and pieces at the bottom of the pot leave it. It’s not burnt. That’s flavor that you want to keep in your pot to make the meal even more flavorful. It will deglaze and cook into the stew once you add your chicken broth.  In the same pot (without washing) on a medium heat add 1-2 TBSP of butter (depending on how much oil or butter you have left from searing the chicken). Add your peppers, onions and seasonings and cook down your peppers and onions for about 8-10 mins or until tender.  Once tender while still on a medium heat add in 1 TBSP of butter and whisk in 2 tbsp of flour to make a roux. Whisk frequently. Don’t walk away from your roux because this is A quick roux and can burn easily so watch it closely.  After about 5 mins you should have the color roux you want your gravy to be. For example if you want a dark brown gravy that roux should be dark brown.  After you’ve achieved that color add in 3 cups of chicken broth 1 cup at a time while stirring in between each cup. Season to taste with named seasonings.  Add in 3-4 crushed garlic cloves and a hefty TBSP of parsley. Put the lid on partially to bring this gravy to a simmer on a medium heat. Marry Me Chicken 🍅✨ A classic dinner idea made a little lighter and packed with protein! This meal is made in one pan and comes together in about 30 minutes. It's the perfect comfort food meal while also helping you hit your protein goals! Makes 4 servings. 4 small chicken breasts (or 2 large cut in half) 1 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp Italian seasoning ½ tsp paprika ½ tsp garlic powder Salt and black pepper, to taste 3 cloves garlic, minced ¾ cup low-sodium chicken broth ⅓ cup chopped sun-dried tomatoes, drained 1 cup low-fat cottage cheese ½ cup fat-free milk ½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese 2 cups fresh spinach Fresh basil, for garnish 1. Blend the cottage cheese and fat-free milk until completely smooth and creamy. 2. Season the chicken with the Italian seasoning, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. 3. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the chicken for 4 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a plate. 4. Reduce the heat to low-medium and cook the garlic for about 30 seconds until fragrant. 5. Pour in the chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Stir in the sun-dried tomatoes and simmer for 2-3 minutes. 6. Remove the skillet from the heat and let cool for about five minutes. 7. Slowly whisk the cottage cheese mixture into the skillet until smooth. (Make sure tomato mixture is cool enough before adding the cottage cheese to prevent curdling!) 8. Add the spinach and cook until wilted. Add Parmesan and mix until melted. 9. Return the chicken to the skillet and warm over low heat for 3-4 minutes. Garnish with fresh basil and enjoy! Serve over pasta, rice, vegetables or bread. #marrymechicken #easydinnerideas #onepanmeal

PAN ROASTED CHICKEN WITH LEEK & TARRAGON BUTTER BEANS 🍗 RECIPE ⬇️ Autumn is officially here, and this is one of my favourite ways to cook chicken - really crisp, golden skin over creamy butter beans cooked with leek, tarragon, and all of the caramelised chicken juices from the pan. The entire dish is made in one pan, from cooking the chicken to going straight back onto the hob for the beans.  RECIPE (serves 2) Pat 2 skin-on chicken supremes dry and season generously with salt. Heat the frying pan over a medium heat, perform the drop test, then add 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the chicken skin-side down and cook for 6-8 minutes until deeply golden and crisp Turn the chicken, then add 30g butter, 3 crushed garlic cloves and 4-5 sprigs of thyme. Once foaming, baste the chicken for 102 minutes, then transfer the chicken to a roasting tray and put in a 200°C fan oven for 10-15 minutes until cooked through. Remove and rest Leave around 1 tbsp of the chicken fat and all the caramelised pan juices behind. Add 2 finely sliced shallots and 1 finely sliced leek with a pinch of salt and cook gently for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add 2 sliced garlic cloves and cook for another minute Add 2 x 400g jars of good quality butter beans, 200ml chicken stock, and 1 tbsp Dijon mustard. Bring to a gentle simmer, then crush some of the beans into the stock to thicken it Turn the heat down and stir through 75g crème fraîche and 15-20g finely grated Parmesan. Once creamy, fold through 2 tbsp fresh tarragon and season with salt and plenty of black pepper Spoon the beans generously onto a plate, place the rested chicken on top and finish with Parmesan and cracked black pepper #chicken #butterbeans #cooking #recipe #autumn

✨ CARAMELIZED BAKED CHICKEN THIGHS ✨ 🍗🍯🧄🔥😍 These caramelized baked chicken thighs are sticky, sweet, and fall-apart tender. Smothered in a rich, glossy glaze that bakes right into the meat, this simple recipe delivers incredible flavor with minimal effort! 🍴 Ingredients: - 8 chicken thighs (bone-in or boneless) - ⅓ cup honey (or maple syrup) - ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce - 2 tbsp brown sugar, packed - 4 cloves garlic, minced - 1 tbsp olive oil - 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar (or fresh lemon juice) - 1 tsp onion powder - 1 tsp smoked paprika - 1 tsp salt - ½ tsp black pepper 👩🏽‍🍳 Instructions: 1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch glass baking dish. 2. Pat the chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt, black pepper, onion powder, and smoked paprika. 3. In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, brown sugar, minced garlic, olive oil, and apple cider vinegar until smooth and well combined. 4. Arrange the seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up in a single layer in the baking dish. 5. Pour the glaze evenly over the chicken, making sure each piece is thoroughly coated. 6. Bake uncovered for 35–40 minutes (for bone-in thighs) or 25–30 minutes (for boneless), basting the chicken with the pan sauce halfway through cooking. 7. Turn the broiler on for the final 2–3 minutes to get that rich, bubbly, caramelized glaze on top (watch closely so it doesn't burn!). 8. Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then spoon the remaining pan juices generously over the top before serving! 📝 Notes: Using bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs keeps the meat exceptionally juicy and gives you the best rich flavor, but boneless skinless thighs work fantastically well too—just reduce the baking time by about 10 minutes. ⏱️ Prep Time: 10 minutes 🍳 Cook Time: 40 minutes ⏰ Total Time: 50 minutes #BakedChickenThighs #CaramelizedChicken #HoneyGarlicChicken #EasyDinner #ChickenRecipes

Creamy Chicken Au Poivre 🍗✨ This might be one of the best ways I’ve ever prepared a whole chicken.  Listen it’s juicy, crispy skin and that creamy peppercorn sauce is EVERYTHINGGG 😮‍💨 thank you @Corre Larkin for sharing this recipe with us! 💕 Interested in trying a Kickin’ Chicken Seasoning Bomb? 👀 I have it linked in the orange cart on this video and in my product showcase.  My version of the viral chicken au poivre: For the chicken: • 1 whole young chicken (4–5 lb), spatchcocked, cleaned and pat dry  • drizzle of good quality olive oil • Salt, to taste For the creamy au poivre sauce:  • 1½ cups heavy cream (I used lactose free) • 2 sprigs fresh rosemary, chopped • 3 cloves garlic, chopped • 1 shallot, sliced • 2 tbsp crushed black peppercorns (more or less, and you can ground the texture as coarse or as fine as you like. This is entirely based on preference since they add a kick) • Generous pinch of salt • ½ Kickin’ Chicken Seasoning Bomb  (optional, yes you can sub with a bouillon cube or seasoning) • Splash of sherry cooking wine How to make it: Pat the chicken dry, massage with olive oil and season with salt on both sides. Roast at 375°F for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, steep the heavy cream with the rosemary, garlic, shallot, cracked peppercorns, salt and ½ Kickin’ Chicken Seasoning Bomb. You want to make sure this is simmering, not boiling, so steam coming from the pot and some *small* bubbles are okay! 👌  Once the 15 minute timer is up, remove the chicken from the oven and pour the creamy au poivre sauce all over. Add a splash of sherry cooking wine and pop it back in the oven to finish roasting at 400 F. Let it roast until the chicken is golden brown and fully cooked through to 165°F.  Save this for your next chicken dinner! 📌🍗 #fy #chickenaupoivre #roastchicken #easyrecipes #dinnerideas
